_note: Which foes a floor fields (§6.2). Every matching table contributes rows and a unit's weight is the sum across them, so a pack adds to the pool by shipping one row and no load order can change the result (§18.6). Depth shaping — the tier cap and the falloff inside it — is applied once afterwards from tuning.spawn, so a themed table cannot accidentally opt out of it.

defs.name: The Wilds
defs._note: The base pool: every unit that describes its own appearance, bosses included — the boss/non-boss split happens when the pool is drawn from, not here, so no table ever has to remember to exclude one. This table is what keeps 'adding a unit is one JSON file and one descriptor' true (the M1 gate): a new unit says where it shows up in its own file and no table needs editing. Themed tables below add on top of it.

defs.name: The Crypt
defs._note: The shallow floors read as a crypt because the Undead are weighted up here, not because anything else is excluded. Weighting rather than filtering is the whole reason a run still surprises you on floor 2.

defs.name: The Deeps
defs._note: Past floor 4 the constructs and drakes take over. The Drake row is the one that makes a Drake-hunting Recruit rule worth writing — and the seam a Bias node (§5) multiplies into.
